fields.description: A rune derived from {{ rules.name }} marks the item; the GM decides its exact function and strength.
The item is visibly damaged; the GM decides whether that has any concrete consequences.
The item comes from a distant age; the GM decides what its history means in play.
The item is associated with {{ affliction }}; the GM decides how the curse manifests.
The item is associated with the {{ status_effect }} status effect; the GM decides how the curse manifests.
The presence of {{ creature.generator.name }} inhabits or influences the item.
The item was made, issued, modified, or marked by {{ faction.name }}.
The item was made, issued, modified, or marked by {{ government.name }}.
The item is aware of its surroundings and has a personality of its own: {{ personality.description }}
The item whispers, sings, rattles, complains, or produces some other unwanted noise at inconvenient moments.
When unattended, the item can crawl, roll, hop, or otherwise relocate itself without warning.
The item reacts to promises, oaths, and agreements made while it is carried or used; the GM decides what it recognizes and how it responds.
The item behaves partly like a living organism: it may grow, heal, eat, sleep, or react when harmed.
The item is supernaturally difficult to conceal completely; some glow, sound, scent, movement, or other telltale sign betrays it.
The item resents similar equipment receiving attention and may complain, interfere, or behave unreliably while its owner uses a rival object.
The item becomes eager and unusually cooperative once serious violence begins, then resists being put away or abandoned before the conflict satisfies it.
The item responds favorably to genuine honesty and becomes cold, obstructive, or unreliable when its owner knowingly lies.
The item becomes more cooperative near the place, culture, maker, magical environment, or material of its origin and less reliable far away.
The item sincerely tries to keep its owner safe, but may resist dangerous journeys, obstruct risky actions, or draw attention to threats against the owner's wishes.
Unfamiliar places, creatures, magic, and objects fascinate the item, which may tug, move, activate, or make noise to encourage investigation.
The item considers its current owner to belong to it and resists being sold, lent, discarded, stolen, or given away.
The item tries to avoid obvious danger by hiding, resisting activation, becoming difficult to draw, attempting to leave, or warning its owner excessively.
